finding.claim: /fetch forwards an attacker-supplied query parameter to http.Get with no validation, and returns the response body to the requester, enabling non-blind SSRF to internal hosts, localhost, and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; response body echoed via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: target read from query string, unmodified
upstream body copied to client response

finding.guards_checked: None. No parsing, scheme check, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, port restriction, or redirect limit. Only err != nil check after the request, which is not a security control. Go client only supports http/https schemes.

verdict.guard_found: none in the /fetch path. main.go:41 routes /fetch to fetch, and fetch (main.go:14-23) has no host, IP, or port check before http.Get at main.go:16. The allowed-host map at main.go:9-12 and the hostname check at main.go:27 belong only to safeFetch, which is registered at main.go:42 on a different route and is not on the /fetch path.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled value from r.URL.Query().Get("target") at main.go:15 reaches http.Get at main.go:16 with no validation, and the body is copied back to the client at main.go:22, so the trace is accurate and the finding holds.

finding.claim: /safe validates only the hostname of the initial URL against an allowlist, but http.Get follows redirects (no CheckRedirect), so an allowlisted host that redirects to an internal address or metadata endpoint lets the requester reach internal resources. Conditional on an allowlisted host (images.example.org or docs.example.org) serving an attacker-influenced redirect, which cannot be confirmed from this repository.
finding.sink: http.Get(u.String()) at main.go:31; final body copied at main.go:37

trace.note: allowed[u.Hostname()] check on initial URL only
http.Get(u.String()) with default client, follows up to 10 redirects, no CheckRedirect
final response body copied to client

finding.guards_checked: Hostname exact-match allowlist on the same parsed value used for the request (no parser differential; u.Hostname() strips port; userinfo and suffix tricks rejected). Scheme not checked but Go client only supports http/https. Port not checked (minor; only reachable on allowlisted hosts). Redirects not validated (the gap). DNS not pinned (only relevant if allowlisted names are attacker-influenced; not the case here).

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 `!allowed[u.Hostname()]`, an exact-match membership check on the parsed hostname of the same URL passed to http.Get at main.go:31. Route registration at main.go:42 and source at main.go:26 match the trace.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate and the source is attacker-controlled, but the exact hostname allowlist at main.go:27 closes the finding per the rubric, and the claimed exploit depends on an allowlisted external host returning a malicious redirect, which this repository cannot show. The unvalidated redirect-following at main.go:31 is a residual hardening gap, not a confirmed SSRF path from this code.
